Consult Summary:
31-year-old man with 4-day history of intensely pruritic, red, cracked rash on chest, hands, and antecubital fossae—consistent with an eczema flare. No systemic symptoms; plan for stronger topical steroid, emollients, and oral antihistamine with review in 1 week.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute flare of eczema/atopic dermatitis over past 4 days.
- Distribution: chest, dorsal hands, antecubital areas; no facial involvement.
- Symptoms: severe itch, soreness, cracked skin; no bleeding, pus, or fever.
- Tried prior prescription eczema cream and OTC mild steroid cream without relief; loratadine (OTC) ineffective.
- Pertinent negatives: no cough, dyspnea, urinary or bowel issues, no recent product/clothing changes identified.
- Impression: eczema exacerbation.

Issue 2:
- Sleep disturbance and impaired daytime concentration secondary to pruritus for 4 days.

Issue 3:
- Past history of asthma (inactive).

Medications:
- OTC mild topical steroid cream (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Loratadine antihistamine (dose/route/frequency not documented) – patient reports minimal benefit.
- New prescriptions: 
  • Stronger topical corticosteroid (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  • Emollient bath/shower wash and moisturizer (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  • Fexofenadine oral antihistamine (dose/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- Denies known drug or environmental allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Atopic eczema.
- Asthma (childhood/past; currently asymptomatic).

Social History:
- Lives with several flat-mates.
- Occupation: project manager in pharmaceutical company.
- Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: a few beers per week, occasional social use.

Preventative History:
- No information provided on immunizations or screening tests.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth visual inspection: rash appears erythematous, dry, and cracked (exact morphology details not documented).
- Vitals not recorded.

Plan:
- Prescribe potent topical steroid for affected areas BID for 7–10 days.
- Prescribe emollient wash/moisturizer for daily use.
- Start Fexofenadine for itch relief.
- Continue to avoid known irritants; maintain diary of possible triggers (soaps, detergents, fabrics).
- Review in 1 week; earlier if worsening, spreading, or signs of infection (pus, fever).
- Consider dermatology referral if no improvement with above regimen.

● No internal conflicts noted.
